evidence.note: Front-loads understanding of the eval harness, checkpoint utils, and renderer, and validates dataset access before committing any training compute — sequencing learning as a distinct first stage rather than jumping to a training run.

Builds separate data/train/eval scripts (build_human_sft_data.py, train_sft_candidate.py, evaluate_llama3.py) before the first fine-tune, establishing distinct train and eval sub-goals rather than one monolithic push.
Each training run has an artifact done-check: verifies checkpoints.jsonl / metrics.jsonl exists before proceeding to evaluation — an explicit per-stage completion criterion.
Evaluates checkpoints (including intermediate ones) as a measurement milestone after training, banking a verified number before continuing.
Iterates through several data variants and hyperparameter settings (rank/LR/steps s260→s200→s160→s80→s60), each as a train→verify-checkpoint→eval cycle rather than a single open-ended run.

reasoning: The agent clearly ordered the campaign into understand-harness → build eval+train tooling → run fine-tune → measure → iterate on data/hparams, with the 45% target as the terminal check and per-run artifact done-checks (checkpoints.jsonl existence before eval), which matches and slightly exceeds the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because there is no evidence of a deliberate tiny end-to-end validation of the eval/checkpoint-writing pipeline before expensive runs, nor explicit numeric go/no-go thresholds stated per stage. That places the observed behavior between the level-5 clear ordered plan and the level-8 risk-first sequencing, i.e. a 6.
